stages.name: Specialisation and trade
stages.title: Specialisation and trade
stages.sub: The gains and risks that come from countries and workers focusing on what they do best.

steps.q: A country that grows coffee well makes only coffee and swaps it for phones, cars and clothes. Does it make everything itself?
steps.right: No, it focuses on coffee and trades for the rest
steps.wrong: Yes, it still tries to make everything itself
steps.hint: Think about what the country actually produces versus what it ends up consuming.

steps.q: A country puts all its land and workers into coffee and trades for phones and clothes. What happens to total output?
steps.right: It rises, resources are used more efficiently
steps.wrong: It falls, resources are spread too thinly
steps.hint: Compare a country splitting its workers across many jobs it is bad at, against putting them all into the one job it is best at.

steps.q: A factory worker tightens the same bolt all day, every day, for years. How does their motivation change?
steps.right: It falls, the repetition becomes dull
steps.wrong: It stays high, repetition keeps skills sharp
steps.hint: Imagine doing the exact same tiny task for eight hours, then again tomorrow, then again next year.

steps.wrong: Yes, their skills transfer to any job
